pillars.name: Practical coding and DSA
pillars.blurb: Multi-stage build-and-extend problems (Anthropic, OpenAI) and classic DSA (Google, Microsoft, Amazon). Python first, TypeScript second.

pillars.name: System design and LLM infrastructure
pillars.blurb: Classic distributed systems plus the LLM-serving, batching, caching, eval-pipeline and agent-orchestration designs every lab asks about.

pillars.name: ML and deep learning fundamentals
pillars.blurb: The breadth-and-depth syllabus Google, Microsoft and Amazon test, and the credibility layer for the labs.

pillars.name: LLM internals and training
pillars.blurb: Transformers from scratch, inference arithmetic, scaling, post-training (SFT, RLHF, DPO), fine-tuning.

pillars.name: LLM application engineering
pillars.blurb: Claude and OpenAI APIs, tool use, agents, MCP, RAG, prompt engineering, context engineering. The Applied AI / FDE implementation round.

pillars.name: Evaluation and observability
pillars.blurb: Eval design, graders, statistics, regression gates, tracing. Reported as the biggest skill gap among AI-engineer candidates.

pillars.name: Safety, alignment and values
pillars.blurb: Primary sources for the Anthropic culture round and OpenAI mission round, plus interpretability for research tracks.

pillars.name: Behavioral, customer conversation, leadership principles
pillars.blurb: STAR/SPSIL stories, Amazon LPs, Microsoft competencies, the FDE discovery conversation.

pillars.name: Applications, networking and India hiring
pillars.blurb: Careers pages, India offices, compensation data, candidate reports, fellowships.

pillars.name: Portfolio and open source
pillars.blurb: Repos to contribute to and the India-domain eval suite that turns your benchmarking job into public evidence.

items.title: NeetCode roadmap and practice
items.why: Structured DSA patterns with video explanations; covers the graph/tree-heavy mix Google and Amazon report.

items.title: Grind 75 (Tech Interview Handbook)
items.why: A time-budgeted LeetCode list you can finish; pairs with the behavioral section of the same handbook.

items.title: LeetCode problem set (company-tagged lists need Premium)
items.why: Google-tagged and Amazon-tagged problems match reported questions closely; DeepMind coaches point at the latest 50 Google-tagged.

items.title: Hello Interview (coding, system design, company guides)
items.why: Has Anthropic and OpenAI level-specific guides and a free system-design course written by ex-FAANG interviewers.

items.title: CodeSignal (Anthropic's 90-minute 4-level screen runs here)
items.why: Get used to the editor, the test-case gating and the clock before the real assessment; practice multi-class Python under time.

items.title: Real Python: Async IO in Python
items.why: Anthropic and OpenAI coding rounds repeatedly ask for concurrent crawlers and ingestion components; asyncio fluency is assumed.

items.title: Python docs: threading, queue, concurrent.futures
items.why: Thread-safe KV stores and lock comparisons were reported at OpenAI; know Lock, RLock, Condition and the GIL tradeoffs cold.

items.title: Fluent Python, 2nd ed. (Ramalho)
items.why: The idiomatic Python the labs grade on: data model, dataclasses, iterators/generators, asyncio, type hints.

items.title: TypeScript Handbook
items.why: OpenAI deployment roles ask for Python and JavaScript; the Agents SDK, MCP SDK and Claude Agent SDK all ship TypeScript.

items.title: Exercism Python track
items.why: Mentored, test-driven exercises that build the clean-code habits reviewers look for in take-homes.

items.title: interviewing.io (anonymous mocks with FAANG/lab engineers)
items.why: Realistic pressure and written feedback; budget 3–4 sessions before real loops.

items.title: Exponent / Aced peer mock interviews
items.why: Free peer mocks for coding, design and behavioral; their company guides are the source for several reported-question lists in the bank.

items.title: Tech Interview Handbook: behavioral interviews
items.why: Compact STAR framework and question list; a good scaffold before you customize for LPs and culture rounds.

items.title: Hello Interview: System Design in a Hurry
items.why: The fastest complete framework for 45-minute design rounds, with delivery guidance and core patterns.

items.title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications (Kleppmann)
items.why: The depth behind every 'why' follow-up: replication, partitioning, consistency, stream processing.

items.title: System Design Primer (GitHub)
items.why: Free reference for the classic building blocks: caches, queues, load balancers, CAP, back-of-envelope math.

items.title: ByteByteGo and the System Design Interview books (Alex Xu)
items.why: Volume 1 covers rate limiters, KV stores, URL shorteners and crawlers, which are exactly the reported shapes.

items.title: Machine Learning System Design Interview (Aminian and Xu)
items.why: Worked answers for recommendation, ranking, ads and moderation systems; matches the Google/Amazon ML design prompts in the bank.

items.title: Designing Machine Learning Systems (Chip Huyen)
items.why: Data pipelines, feature stores, monitoring and drift, the production vocabulary Amazon and Microsoft design rounds expect.

items.title: AI Engineering (Chip Huyen)
items.why: The best single book on building with foundation models: evals, RAG, agents, fine-tuning decisions, inference optimization.

items.title: Machine-Learning-Interviews repo (alirezadir), 2026 GenAI chapters
items.why: ML system design templates plus 2026 chapters on LLM internals, post-training and GenAI system design.

items.title: Eugene Yan: Patterns for Building LLM-based Systems and Products
items.why: Evals, RAG, fine-tuning, caching, guardrails and UX as a connected set of patterns; a design-round vocabulary in one post.

items.title: Lilian Weng: Large Transformer Model Inference Optimization
items.why: Quantization, pruning, distillation, KV caching and parallelism in one survey; the background for serving-stack design questions.

items.title: Transformer Inference Arithmetic (kipply)
items.why: Teaches the back-of-envelope KV-cache and FLOP math that design interviewers at the labs probe.

items.title: vLLM documentation (paged attention, continuous batching)
items.why: Know how a real serving engine schedules prefill and decode before you design one on a whiteboard.

items.title: Anyscale: continuous batching for LLM inference
items.why: The 'batched inference system where 100 requests cost the same as 1' question, explained with measurements.

items.title: How to Scale Your Model (Google DeepMind JAX scaling book)
items.why: Rooflines, parallelism and TPU/GPU systems thinking from the people who train Gemini; research-engineer depth.

items.title: Machine Learning Specialization (Andrew Ng, Coursera)
items.why: Still the cleanest grounding in regression, classification, regularization and bias/variance that breadth rounds test.

items.title: Deep Learning Specialization (DeepLearning.AI)
items.why: Optimization, regularization, CNNs, sequence models and the 'why ReLU / what if you remove hidden layers' style questions.

items.title: Stanford CS229: Machine Learning (notes and lectures)
items.why: Derivations: closed-form linear regression, logistic loss convexity, MLE vs Bayesian; Amazon's breadth round in course form.

items.title: fast.ai: Practical Deep Learning for Coders
items.why: Top-down, code-first deep learning; good if theory-first courses stall you.

items.title: 3Blue1Brown: Neural networks (incl. transformers and attention)
items.why: Visual intuition for backprop and attention that makes the whiteboard explanations land.

items.title: StatQuest (Josh Starmer)
items.why: Precision/recall, ROC, regularization, boosting, cross-validation, each in ten minutes; breadth-round flashcards in video form.

items.title: Dive into Deep Learning (d2l.ai)
items.why: Runnable notebooks for every architecture; implement attention, batch norm and convolution in pure code as Google coaches suggest.

items.title: Understanding Deep Learning (Simon Prince)
items.why: Modern, free, rigorous; the chapters on transformers, diffusion and RL are current.

items.title: Deep Learning (Goodfellow, Bengio, Courville)
items.why: The reference DeepMind's 'quiz' round is calibrated against.

items.title: Mathematics for Machine Learning
items.why: Linear algebra, probability and optimization at exactly the depth needed to derive things live.

items.title: Information Theory, Inference, and Learning Algorithms (MacKay)
items.why: OpenAI research-engineer loops reportedly weave information theory into coding rounds; this is the canonical free text.

items.title: Google Machine Learning Crash Course
items.why: Google's own framing of ML fundamentals, including the production and fairness modules.

items.title: The Elements of Statistical Learning
items.why: Bagging vs boosting, regularization paths and kernel methods at the depth applied-scientist loops sometimes reach.

items.title: Seeing Theory (visual probability and statistics)
items.why: Quick refresh on distributions, Bayes and confidence intervals before A/B-test and eval-statistics questions.

items.title: MIT 6.S191: Introduction to Deep Learning
items.why: Updated yearly with LLM and agent lectures; compact review of the whole stack.

items.title: Andrej Karpathy: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
items.why: Backprop, makemore, GPT and the tokenizer from scratch; the single best preparation for 'implement attention' rounds.

items.title: Karpathy: Let's reproduce GPT-2 (124M)
items.why: Training-loop engineering, mixed precision, distributed data parallel; the research-engineer debugging round in video form.

items.title: Karpathy: Deep Dive into LLMs like ChatGPT
items.why: Pretraining, SFT, RLHF, hallucinations and tool use end to end; the mental model every interviewer assumes.

items.title: nanoGPT and nanochat (Karpathy)
items.why: Read, run and modify a full train-to-chat pipeline; OpenAI's transformer-debugging round assumes you can.

items.title: Stanford CS336: Language Modeling from Scratch
items.why: Assignments build a tokenizer, model, optimizer, data pipeline and eval; the deepest public LLM-engineering course.

items.title: Stanford CS224N: NLP with Deep Learning
items.why: Attention, transformers, pretraining and RLHF lectures with assignments; the standard NLP syllabus.

items.title: Stanford CS25: Transformers United
items.why: Guest lectures from the people who built the models; good for 'where is the field going' conversations.

items.title: The Illustrated Transformer (Jay Alammar)
items.why: The diagram you will draw on the whiteboard.

items.title: Attention Is All You Need (2017)
items.why: Read it once properly; interviewers ask why the square-root scaling, why LayerNorm, why positional encodings.

items.title: Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch) (Raschka)
items.why: Step-by-step PyTorch with the code open-sourced; includes KV cache and fine-tuning chapters.

items.title: Hugging Face LLM Course
items.why: Tokenizers, fine-tuning and the Transformers library hands-on.

items.title: Hands-On Large Language Models (Alammar and Grootendorst)
items.why: Visual, practical coverage of embeddings, semantic search, generation and fine-tuning.

items.title: RLHF Book (Nathan Lambert)
items.why: Reward models, PPO, DPO, rejection sampling and RLVR explained by a practitioner; Anthropic RE rounds ask about PPO mechanics.

items.title: Illustrating RLHF (Hugging Face)
items.why: Ten-minute version of the post-training pipeline for behavioral and values conversations.

items.title: InstructGPT paper (Training LMs to follow instructions with human feedback)
items.why: The RLHF recipe that made ChatGPT; read alongside the Constitutional AI paper.

items.title: Direct Preference Optimization
items.why: Know when DPO replaces PPO and what it gives up.

items.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models and Chinchilla
items.why: Anthropic RE candidates were asked how scaling laws affect safety evaluation.

items.title: FlashAttention paper
items.why: Why attention is memory-bound and how tiling fixes it; a frequent follow-up in serving-design rounds.

items.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation
items.why: You list LoRA/QLoRA on your profile; be able to explain the math and the tradeoffs in two minutes.

items.title: Transformer Math 101 (EleutherAI)
items.why: Compute and memory formulas for training and inference; pairs with kipply's inference post.

items.title: The Ultra-Scale Playbook: training LLMs on GPU clusters (Hugging Face)
items.why: Data, tensor, pipeline and expert parallelism with real measurements; the Amazon AGI and OpenAI RE design questions.

items.title: Lilian Weng: The Transformer Family v2
items.why: Positional encodings, sparse attention, RoPE and long-context variants in one survey.

items.title: Umar Jamil (YouTube): attention, LLaMA, RLHF coded from scratch
items.why: Long-form code-alongs that go deeper than Karpathy on RoPE, KV cache, GQA and PPO.

items.title: Claude Developer Platform documentation
items.why: Tool use, structured outputs, prompt caching, Batches, extended thinking, Files, Agent SDK. Know every page before an Anthropic loop.

items.title: Claude prompt engineering guide
items.why: Anthropic's own prompting techniques; the FDE use-case screen watches how you prompt.

items.title: Anthropic courses (GitHub): API fundamentals, prompting, evals, tool use
items.why: Five notebook courses written by Anthropic, including a prompt-evaluations course.

items.title: Anthropic Cookbook
items.why: Runnable recipes for RAG, tool use, agents, PDFs and more; a merged PR here is strong signal.

items.title: Anthropic: Building effective agents
items.why: The house style for agent design: simple composable workflows before autonomous agents. Design answers aligned with it land.

items.title: Anthropic: Writing effective tools for agents
items.why: Tool schemas, descriptions and result formatting; directly relevant to the MCP use-case screen.

items.title: Anthropic: Effective context engineering for AI agents
items.why: Context budgets, compaction, memory and sub-agents; the vocabulary of long-running-agent design questions.

items.title: Claude Code best practices
items.why: Use Claude Code seriously for a week on a real project; 'here's where the harness helped and fell over' is a strong talking point.

items.title: Claude Agent SDK documentation
items.why: Build one sub-agent workflow with it; FDE job descriptions list sub-agents and agent skills as deliverables.

items.title: Model Context Protocol documentation
items.why: Anthropic's FDE technical screen is built around an MCP scenario; Microsoft's agent-host design question includes MCP tools.

items.title: MCP reference servers (GitHub)
items.why: Read two servers, then write your own over KaatDo's broker abstraction or Ahead's source registry.

items.title: DeepLearning.AI: MCP: Build Rich-Context AI Apps with Anthropic
items.why: Short, hands-on introduction co-built with Anthropic.

items.title: OpenAI API documentation (Responses API, tools, structured outputs)
items.why: Know Responses, function calling, structured outputs, Batch, evals and fine-tuning endpoints before an OpenAI applied loop.

items.title: OpenAI Cookbook
items.why: Reference implementations for RAG, evals, agents and fine-tuning in OpenAI's idiom; contribution target.

items.title: OpenAI Agents SDK documentation
items.why: Handoffs, guardrails, tracing and sessions; build the same agent you built on Claude, then compare.

items.title: OpenAI: A practical guide to building agents (PDF)
items.why: OpenAI's own framing of when to build an agent, orchestration patterns and guardrails; quote it in the FDE round.

items.title: OpenAI Academy
items.why: Free learning hub, expanding in India via certifications; useful for the India GTM conversations too.

items.title: DeepLearning.AI short courses (RAG, agents, evals, post-training)
items.why: One-to-two-hour courses co-built with Anthropic, OpenAI, LangChain and others; pick the evals and agents ones first.

items.title: Hugging Face Agents Course
items.why: Framework-agnostic agents, tools, memory and evaluation with a final project.

items.title: Full Stack LLM Bootcamp (Full Stack Deep Learning)
items.why: Older but still the best single day on LLMOps, UX and augmented LMs.

items.title: Prompt Engineering Guide (promptingguide.ai)
items.why: Catalog of techniques with papers; good for 'talk about prompt engineering principles'.

items.title: Google: Prompt Engineering whitepaper (Kaggle)
items.why: Google's own prompting guidance, useful for Google Cloud AI engineering conversations.

items.title: Google: Agents whitepaper (Kaggle)
items.why: Google's agent architecture vocabulary (orchestration layer, tools, extensions).

items.title: Gemini API documentation
items.why: Build the same reference agent on Gemini to speak credibly about model differences.

items.title: Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore documentation
items.why: Your bridge: Claude on Bedrock is how most Indian enterprises buy it. Bedrock Agents, Guardrails and Knowledge Bases map to AWS GenAI SA roles.

items.title: Azure AI Foundry documentation
items.why: Microsoft AI engineer rounds push on Azure AI Search, Foundry evaluators and Copilot-stack realities.

items.title: LangGraph documentation
items.why: You already ship LangGraph at Amazon; be able to explain its durable-execution and state model versus a plain loop.

items.title: Simon Willison: prompt injection series
items.why: Every lab asks a prompt-injection defense question; this series is the clearest treatment, including the dual-LLM pattern.

items.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
items.why: A shared checklist for the security half of enterprise deployment questions.

items.title: Hamel Husain: Your AI Product Needs Evals
items.why: The eval-driven development loop (unit tests, human review, LLM judge) that interviewers want to hear.

items.title: Hamel Husain and Shreya Shankar: LLM evals FAQ
items.why: Answers the exact follow-ups you will get: judge calibration, sample sizes, binary vs Likert, when to fine-tune the judge.

items.title: Eugene Yan: Task-specific LLM evals that do and don't work
items.why: Concrete metrics for classification, summarization, translation and toxicity tasks.

items.title: Anthropic: A statistical approach to model evaluations
items.why: Standard errors, clustering and paired differences for eval scores; 'how large must the eval set be to trust a 3-point gap' answered.

items.title: Claude docs: Define success criteria and develop test cases
items.why: Anthropic's own eval-design guidance, including grader types.

items.title: Inspect AI (UK AISI) documentation
items.why: The eval framework to build your India-domain suite on; used by labs and governments, with agentic eval support.

items.title: lm-evaluation-harness (EleutherAI)
items.why: The standard open benchmark runner; add a task to it as an OSS contribution.

items.title: OpenAI Evals (GitHub)
items.why: Registry format and templates for evals in OpenAI's idiom.

items.title: HELM (Stanford CRFM)
items.why: Holistic evaluation methodology and leaderboards; a reference when designing your own suite.

items.title: LMArena (Chatbot Arena)
items.why: Know how pairwise human preference leaderboards work and their limitations.

items.title: Epoch AI benchmarking hub
items.why: Independent, dated benchmark results across frontier models for 'where is the field' conversations.

items.title: Langfuse documentation (open-source LLM tracing and evals)
items.why: Instrument your flagship agent with traces, scores and datasets so you can show observability, not describe it.

items.title: Arize Phoenix documentation (open-source observability)
items.why: OpenTelemetry-based LLM tracing and eval runs; alternative to Langfuse.

items.title: Anthropic: Core Views on AI Safety
items.why: The document the culture round assumes you have read. Write down one argument you find weak.

items.title: Anthropic: Responsible Scaling Policy
items.why: ASL levels, capability thresholds and safeguards; be able to say what you would change.

items.title: Claude's constitution
items.why: Read the current constitution linked from Anthropic news; the 2026 revision moved from a principle list to explained reasoning with a priority order.

items.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
items.why: 'Explain Constitutional AI and what it doesn't solve' is a reported-style question.

items.title: Anthropic: Alignment faking in large language models
items.why: The deceptive-alignment concern made concrete; the kind of result to have an informed opinion about.

items.title: Anthropic: Agentic misalignment
items.why: Insider-threat style behaviors in agentic settings; directly relevant to enterprise agent deployment judgment.

items.title: Anthropic: Mapping the mind of a large language model
items.why: Sparse autoencoders and features; the interpretability result to cite and question.

items.title: A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits
items.why: Induction heads and circuits; the background for Anthropic's mech-interp take-home.

items.title: Neel Nanda: getting started in mechanistic interpretability
items.why: Concrete starter projects; one finished mech-interp notebook is research-track evidence.

items.title: ARENA (Alignment Research Engineer Accelerator) curriculum
items.why: Open curriculum: transformers from scratch, mech interp, RL and evals. The stretch-path syllabus.

items.title: BlueDot Impact: AI Safety Fundamentals courses
items.why: Structured reading groups on alignment and governance; the fastest way to form defensible views for values rounds.

items.title: OpenAI Charter
items.why: 'Which parts of the mission resonate' is a reported question; know the charter's commitments and where you'd probe them.

items.title: OpenAI: Preparedness Framework (2025 update)
items.why: OpenAI's counterpart to the RSP; compare the two in your written notes.

items.title: OpenAI Model Spec
items.why: How OpenAI wants models to behave, including the instruction hierarchy; relevant to prompt-injection and behavior questions.

items.title: Dario Amodei: Machines of Loving Grace
items.why: The 'light' half of light and shade; shows you engage with the upside case, not only the risks.

items.title: Dario Amodei: The Urgency of Interpretability
items.why: Why Anthropic bets on interpretability; a good place to locate your own disagreement.

items.title: Google DeepMind: Taking a responsible path to AGI (technical AGI safety approach)
items.why: DeepMind's framing of misuse, misalignment and oversight for 'why this lab' conversations.

items.title: Concrete Problems in AI Safety (2016)
items.why: Reward hacking, safe exploration and distributional shift; still the shared vocabulary.

items.title: AI Alignment Forum
items.why: Where alignment researchers argue in public; read the curated posts, not everything.

items.title: 80,000 Hours: risks from AI problem profile and career guides
items.why: Balanced overview of the risk arguments and the career paths into safety work.

items.title: Anthropic: company and values page
items.why: The seven values (act for the global good, hold light and shade, do the simple thing that works...). The culture round scores against them.

items.title: Amazon Leadership Principles
items.why: Every Amazon interviewer grades two or three LPs with STAR questions; map your 8–10 stories to them.

items.title: Amazon: Applied Scientist interview prep (official)
items.why: Official loop shape: 1–2 phone screens, four 55-minute interviews, LPs in every round, no brain teasers.

items.title: Amazon: Interviewing at Amazon (official hub)
items.why: Official guidance on STAR, the Bar Raiser and the loop; use for internal moves too.

items.title: Google: How we hire
items.why: Google's own description of GCA, RRK, leadership and Googleyness.

items.title: Anthropic: Guidance on candidates' AI usage
items.why: Draft applications yourself then refine with Claude; no AI in take-homes or live rounds unless told. Candidates have reportedly been dropped for violating it.

items.title: IGotAnOffer: Anthropic culture interview guide
items.why: Reported culture-round questions grouped into five types, with the seven values quoted.

items.title: IGotAnOffer: OpenAI behavioral interview guide
items.why: Reported OpenAI behavioral and mission questions with answer structure.

items.title: The Mom Test (Rob Fitzpatrick)
items.why: How to run a discovery conversation that gets facts instead of politeness; the skill the FDE customer simulation grades.

items.title: Exponent: Forward Deployed Engineer interview, the definitive 2026 guide
items.why: Round-by-round shape of FDE loops at the labs and Palantir, including the customer-scenario round.

items.title: Aced: Anthropic FDE interview guide (reported rounds)
items.why: Reported hiring-manager questions (why ML/LLM fit, adoption, time to production) and the MCP use-case screen.

items.title: Anthropic careers
items.why: Filter by Bengaluru and by Applied AI; the Jobs page on this site watches the same Greenhouse board.

items.title: Anthropic opens Bengaluru office (Feb 2026)
items.why: Names the India partnerships (Karya, Collective Intelligence Project evals in agriculture and law) your flagship project should speak to.

items.title: OpenAI careers search
items.why: Filter by India locations; AI Deployment Engineer and Applied AI Engineer roles post here.

items.title: Introducing OpenAI for India
items.why: OpenAI's India strategy (offices, certifications with TCS, partnerships); context for recruiter and mission conversations.

items.title: Google careers (ML and AI roles, India)
items.why: No public JSON feed, so this link is the manual check from the Jobs page.

items.title: Google DeepMind careers
items.why: Research Engineer roles are mostly London/MTV; Bengaluru has a small DeepMind presence.

items.title: Microsoft careers (AI roles, India)
items.why: Hyderabad and Bengaluru AI engineering and applied-scientist roles.

items.title: Amazon jobs: generative AI roles in India
items.why: Internal mobility into a Bedrock/GenAI SA or applied role is the stepping stone named in the roadmap.

items.title: Levels.fyi: Anthropic compensation
items.why: Calibrate levels and offers; India bands differ from US bands.

items.title: Levels.fyi: OpenAI compensation
items.why: Calibrate OpenAI levels and offers; India bands differ from US bands.

items.title: Glassdoor: Anthropic interview reports
items.why: Primary source for most reported questions in the bank; read the newest 20 before a loop.

items.title: Glassdoor: OpenAI interview reports
items.why: Primary source for the OpenAI reported questions; read the newest 20 before a loop.

items.title: Blind (anonymous tech community)
items.why: Candid loop reports and team-matching timelines; filter the noise.

items.title: OpenAI Developer Community
items.why: Answer questions there; visible, verifiable helpfulness.

items.title: Anthropic Fellows Program (AI safety research, 4 months, paid)
items.why: Funded, mentored research fellowship with rolling applications and a high conversion rate to full-time; the stretch path if the eval suite turns into research.

items.title: MATS (ML Alignment and Theory Scholars)
items.why: Mentored alignment research program whose alumni are hired across the labs.

items.title: IGotAnOffer: Anthropic software engineer interview (45 reports analyzed)
items.why: Process, timeline and reported questions; the source of most of the Anthropic coding list in the bank.

items.title: IGotAnOffer: 30+ OpenAI interview questions by role
items.why: Reported coding, design, behavioral, RE, SA and FDE questions.

items.title: AI-Engineer-Interview-Questions repo (ombharatiya), company files
items.why: Per-company loop maps for all five companies plus worked representative answers; reviewed October 2026.

items.title: awesome-ai-engineer-interview (landedjobs)
items.why: Reported questions with provenance tags; the Anthropic file lists a mech-interp take-home.

items.title: anthropic-sdk-python (contribution target)
items.why: Docs, tests and small fixes first; one real bug with a reproducible test later.

items.title: openai-agents-python (contribution target)
items.why: Active, example-heavy repo where a well-tested example or bug fix is realistic.

items.title: inspect_ai (contribution target)
items.why: Build the India-domain suite as an Inspect task set and upstream the generic pieces.

items.title: AI4Bharat (IIT Madras): Indic datasets, models and benchmarks
items.why: Datasets and benchmarks (IndicXTREME, MILU) to build your Indic eval suite on, and the community to share it with.

items.title: IndicGenBench (Google Research)
items.why: Google's multilingual Indic generation benchmark; a baseline to compare your suite against.

items.title: MILU: Multi-task Indic Language Understanding benchmark (AI4Bharat)
items.why: Shows what an India-domain knowledge benchmark looks like; extend into agriculture, law and health workflows.

items.title: Karya (Anthropic's India evals partner)
items.why: Understand the partner building Anthropic's India evaluations; your suite is adjacent work.

items.title: Anthropic: Designing AI-resistant technical evaluations (open take-home challenge)
items.why: Anthropic released its performance-engineering take-home as an open challenge; a strong public signal if you do well. Optional.

items.title: Hugging Face Hub (publish your eval datasets and results)
items.why: Host the eval dataset and a leaderboard Space so the flagship is reproducible and citable.
